definition: Impervious means impossible to penetrate, damage, or affect, usually by one specific thing, and it is most often followed by the word to.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impervious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impervious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The bank's vault door is impervious to drills and cutting torches, which is why its basic design has not changed in forty years.
Resistant is weaker than impervious; a resistant surface holds up against damage for a while, but an impervious one is not affected at all.
Invulnerable is stronger than impervious; impervious usually means unaffected by one specific thing, while invulnerable means impossible to harm in any way at all.

Impenetrable describes the barrier itself — a wall, a vault, a defense that nothing can find a way through. Impervious describes how something stands toward one specific force, and usually takes to: impervious to water, impervious to criticism. Armor is impenetrable; the knight inside is impervious to arrows.

Unaffected simply reports an outcome — something happened and left no mark this time. Impervious makes a stronger, standing claim: the thing cannot be penetrated or affected by that force at all. A speaker might be unaffected by one heckler yet not truly impervious to heckling.

Immune means protected by one's own makeup, the way a vaccinated body is immune to a virus, and it also takes to, as in immune to flattery. Immune stresses built-in protection; impervious stresses that the force simply cannot penetrate or touch the thing at all.

During the championship debate, hecklers in the back row shouted through Amara's entire speech, but she was impervious to the noise and never once lost her place.
The shouting was meant to rattle Amara, yet it had no effect on her at all.
Being unable to be affected or penetrated by something, in this case the heckling, is the core meaning of impervious.
Almost always followed by to: impervious to water, impervious to criticism, impervious to cold.
Do not confuse it with oblivious, which means unaware; an impervious person notices the insults and simply is not affected by them.
